prompt:
Base rules. A change that breaks any of these is rejected before scoring:
1. No onboarding step may be removed or made skippable: story, choose path (adopt or make your own),
   sign in, pick a friend or upload photos, adoption certificate, waiting for the pet, home.
   Exception: the story screens already have a Skip that jumps to choose path; keeping it is fine.
2. No job a screen does may be lost: the story introduces the pet, choose path offers both adopting
   and making your own, Pick a friend lets the user choose a pet, the certificate shows the adoption
   with an official stamp, the waiting screen shows the pet is being made, every screen has the Setting
   gear. Any design may be replaced by a better one, as long as it still does the same job.
3. Pricing stays as it is: the first adoption is free and later adoptions are paid. Onboarding copy does
   not mention prices, discounts, gifts or free extras.
4. Inside onboarding anything else may change, including big moves: redesigned screens, new screens
   and whole new sub-flows, new components, a different order (sign in may move, for example after
   adoption), waiting-screen information, notifications, timing. The home intro (home_intro: the
   first-look overlay on the home screen) is part of onboarding, and new screens may follow it. Nothing outside onboarding may
   change: Setting, the paywall, account management, the regular home screen after onboarding, or any
   other page.
5. Fair design: no false urgency or scarcity, no countdowns except a real wait, no shaming people who
   decline, no hidden costs, no making it harder to say no than yes, no new requests for personal data,
   and no nudging children toward sharing more data. (FTC dark-patterns report; EU DSA Art. 25; EU AI
   Act Art. 5; UK Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 13.)

Check each proposed change against the base rules. Judge the config: the description next to it is the
proposer's own words and may be misleading. Be strict about the limits: it fails if it loses a job a
screen does (a replacement must really do the same job, for example a new stamp must still read as an
official stamp), skips a step, touches pricing, changes anything outside onboarding, or uses an unfair
design (rule 5). Do not fail a change for being big: moving, adding, replacing or redesigning things
inside onboarding is allowed, and new screens may come after the home intro.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "pass": true or false, "rule": rule number or null, "reason": short}]}

Changes (with their configs):

   config: {"choose_path": {"layout": "two_column", "headline": "Choose How You Want to Adopt Your Pet", "body": "Select a ready-made desktop companion or upload your own pet photo to create a custom companion."}}

   config: {"sign_in": {"layout": "card", "headline": "Sign In to Your Desktop Companion Account", "body": "Logging in ensures your pet data, custom creations, and settings are preserved across sessions."}}

   config: {"pick_friend": {"layout": "carousel", "headline": "Browse Desktop Companions", "body": "Swipe or click through available pet models to find the companion that fits your desktop best."}}
3: [home, redesign] Stage Layout Generation Wait View: Redesign the waiting screen into a focused stage layout centered around the pet companion creation status.
   config: {"waiting": {"layout": "stage", "headline": "Your Pet Companion is Arriving", "body": "Please hold on while we build and configure your companion for your desktop workspace."}}

   config: {"home_intro": {"layout": "split", "headline": "Your Pet is Active on Your Desktop", "body": "Your desktop companion is ready. Review quick interaction options on the right before getting started."}}

   config: {"upload_photos": {"layout": "compact", "headline": "Upload Pet Photo", "body": "Select a clear front-facing photo of your pet for best custom model results."}}

   config: {"story": {"headline": "Your Always-On Desktop Companion", "body": "Adopt or create an interactive companion that lives directly on your desktop screen while you work."}}
7: [adoption, incentive] Adoption Certificate Name Customization Stamp: Replace certificate elements with an interactive pet name input component and an official adoption badge.
   config: {"adoption_certificate": {"replace": {"certificate": [{"role": "certificate", "type": "name_input", "label": "Name Your Pet", "style": "rounded", "text": "Enter companion name"}, {"role": "certificate", "type": "badge", "label": "Official Adoption Certificate", "style": "emphasis"}]}}}
8: [sign_in, copy] Sign In Clear Re-authentication Copy: Update sign_in headline and body copy to explicitly instruct existing users on how to recover existing pets during sign-in.
   config: {"sign_in": {"headline": "Sign In to Restore Existing Pets", "body": "Log into your account to access your saved desktop companions and sync existing data."}}
9: [finish, layout] Home Intro Checklist Layout: Change home_intro screen to a checklist layout highlighting key shortcuts and interaction toggles.

verdicts.reason: Redesigns choose_path into a two-column layout while preserving all jobs and steps.
Redesigns sign_in into a card layout while maintaining sign-in functionality.
Redesigns pick_friend into a carousel layout without losing the ability to pick a pet.
Redesigns waiting screen while clearly showing the pet is being created.
Redesigns home_intro into a split layout within onboarding rules.
Reformats photo upload screen layout cleanly while retaining photo upload functionality.
Updates story copy while preserving its job of introducing the pet companion concept.
Replacing certificate elements with a badge removes the required official stamp from the adoption certificate.
Updates sign_in copy to assist returning users without violating any rules.
Changes home_intro to a checklist layout within onboarding bounds.
